setups.name: Pullback in an uptrend
setups.rule: Price above its 200-day average, but RSI(14) below 35
setups.explain: A stock in a long-term uptrend has had a sharp short-term drop. Some traders look for these as 'buy the dip' candidates; the risk is that the drop is the start of a bigger fall.

setups.name: Bounce off the lower Bollinger Band
setups.rule: Closed below the lower Bollinger Band yesterday, back above it today
setups.explain: The price was unusually low compared with its last 20 days and has just turned back up. A classic mean-reversion signal.

setups.name: MACD bullish crossover
setups.rule: MACD crossed above its signal line in the last 3 days, price above 200-day average
setups.explain: Short-term momentum has turned up inside a long-term uptrend. A trend-following signal.

setups.name: Bollinger squeeze
setups.rule: Bollinger Bands at their narrowest 10% of the last 6 months
setups.explain: The stock has gone unusually quiet. Quiet periods are often followed by a bigger move, but the signal doesn't say which direction.

setups.name: Breakout to a 52-week high
setups.rule: Closed above every close of the previous 251 trading days
setups.explain: Momentum: stocks making new highs have no sellers 'stuck' above them. Often keeps going, but can also mark a top.

setups.name: Overbought and stretched
setups.rule: RSI(14) above 75 and price above the upper Bollinger Band
setups.explain: The stock has run up very fast. Not a sell signal on its own, but chasing it here carries higher risk of a pullback.

setups.name: MACD bearish crossover in a downtrend
setups.rule: MACD crossed below its signal line in the last 3 days, price below 200-day average
setups.explain: Short-term momentum has turned down inside a long-term downtrend. Traders who short look for these; holders may see it as a warning.
